task: Check selected sites for public profiles using a username

x-display.title: Find where a username is used
x-display.summary: Check the sites you choose and save a spreadsheet-friendly report of matches and failed checks.
x-display.description:
Look for your old accounts or check where a username appears publicly. Supply one or more usernames and choose the sites to check. The report keeps the profile links, each site’s response and any checks that could not complete.

A matching username does not establish who owns an account. Sherlock can produce false matches when sites change their pages or block automated requests; use the links to check the result.

packaging_note: Uses the pinned upstream Python API and site definitions. Keeps output filenames fixed and distinguishes blocked/server-error requests from negative matches; does not use the CLI's username-derived output paths.

inputs.what: a folder containing search.json with usernames and sites arrays, optional timeout (1–60 seconds) and nsfw (false by default); optionally add sites.json with custom Sherlock definitions

outputs.what: one row per username and site, including profile URL, reported result and HTTP status
the complete structured report, including unavailable checks

access.why: Check the public sites you choose and read upstream's current false-positive exclusions.

known_issues: Use this for public profiles you have a reason to check. Results do not identify a person or prove account ownership.
403, 429, server errors and failed connections are marked unavailable, not absent. A run where no site can give a usable response fails.
Sites change their detection rules. A pinned site definition can become stale even when installation still works. Custom definitions let your agent configure a site without changing the runtime.
